title: Complex thermoelectric materials
why: The most-cited modern introduction to zT, phonon-glass/electron-crystal and the design strategies (complex cells, nanostructuring) behind every family in this atlas.

ref.title: Complex thermoelectric materials

title: A practical field guide to thermoelectrics
why: Written for experimentalists entering the field. Covers synthesis, densification, characterization and the common measurement pitfalls.

ref.title: A practical field guide to thermoelectrics: Fundamentals, synthesis, and characterization

title: Measuring thermoelectric transport properties of materials
why: Rigorous reference on measuring Seebeck coefficient, resistivity, thermal diffusivity and Hall effect, with error budgets. Read it before you report a zT.

ref.title: Measuring thermoelectric transport properties of materials

title: Colloquium: Topological insulators
why: The standard entry point to Z2 topological insulators, from theory to ARPES.

ref.title: Colloquium : Topological insulators

title: Topological insulators and superconductors
why: Field-theoretical companion to Hasan & Kane, including the axion response.

ref.title: Topological insulators and superconductors

title: Topological insulator materials
why: A materials- and transport-oriented review: defect chemistry, bulk-insulating compositions and how to identify surface transport.

ref.title: Topological Insulator Materials
ref.journal: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan

title: Tetradymites as thermoelectrics and topological insulators
why: The one review that covers both applications of this atlas for the same material family. Highly recommended.

ref.title: Tetradymites as thermoelectrics and topological insulators

title: Weyl and Dirac semimetals in three-dimensional solids
why: Comprehensive review of topological semimetals, including magneto-transport signatures.

ref.title: Weyl and Dirac semimetals in three-dimensional solids

title: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and its application to topological materials
why: How ARPES is used to identify Dirac cones, Fermi arcs and band inversions.

ref.title: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and its application to topological materials

title: Angle-resolved photoemission studies of quantum materials
why: In-depth modern treatment of the ARPES technique, its matrix elements and its limits.

ref.title: Angle-resolved photoemission studies of quantum materials

title: Topological quantum chemistry
why: Connects crystal symmetry (space groups, Wyckoff positions) to band topology. It is the basis of today's topological materials catalogues.

ref.title: Topological quantum chemistry

title: A complete catalogue of high-quality topological materials
why: High-throughput symmetry-indicator screening of the ICSD; useful for finding candidates.

ref.title: A complete catalogue of high-quality topological materials

title: High-throughput discovery of topologically non-trivial materials using spin-orbit spillage
why: Explains the spillage indicator shown on every material page in this atlas.

ref.title: High-throughput Discovery of Topologically Non-trivial Materials using Spin-orbit Spillage

title: Data-driven discovery of 3D and 2D thermoelectric materials
why: Methodology behind the BoltzTraP Seebeck/power-factor values displayed here.

ref.title: Data-driven discovery of 3D and 2D thermoelectric materials

title: Topology in Condensed Matter (online course, TU Delft)
why: A free, interactive course with runnable notebooks, from Berry phases to TIs, Weyl semimetals and Majoranas. The best structured self-study path.

title: Thermoelectrics at Northwestern (Snyder group)
why: Educational pages on transport theory, the effective-mass model, the weighted mobility and measurement practice from a leading experimental group.

title: nanoHUB — Thermoelectricity resources
why: Lectures and online simulation tools on thermoelectric transport.

title: Berry Phases in Electronic Structure Theory (Vanderbilt)
why: The definitive textbook on polarization, Berry phases and topological invariants from first principles.

ref.title: Berry Phases in Electronic Structure Theory

title: Introduction to Thermoelectricity (Goldsmid)
why: A classic, accessible textbook by a pioneer of Bi2Te3 thermoelectrics.

ref.title: Introduction to Thermoelectricity

title: VESTA — 3D visualization of crystal structures
why: Opens the CIF files you download here and simulates powder XRD patterns to compare with your own.

title: pymatgen — Python Materials Genomics
why: Read, analyse and transform the structures from this atlas in Python.

title: Robocrystallographer — automatic text descriptions of crystal structures
why: Generates the "Structure in words" paragraph on every exhibit: coordination environments, polyhedral connectivity, bond lengths and dimensionality. Run it on your own refined CIFs to get a consistent first description.

ref.title: Robocrystallographer: automated crystal structure text descriptions and analysis

title: Crystal-GENUI — coordination polyhedra and crystal-chemistry analysis
why: Powers the coordination-polyhedra panel: polyhedron types, distortion indices, bond-valence sums, Pauling-rule checks and an interactive polyhedral viewer, with CSV export for your own refinements.

title: ASE — Atomic Simulation Environment
why: Build supercells, surfaces and defect models and drive most DFT codes.

title: BoltzTraP2 — Boltzmann transport from band structures
why: Standard tool for computing Seebeck coefficients and σ/τ from DFT bands.

ref.title: BoltzTraP2, a program for interpolating band structures and calculating semi-classical transport coefficients

title: AMSET — ab initio carrier scattering and transport
why: Goes beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation, which matters for quantitative mobility and zT.

ref.title: Efficient calculation of carrier scattering rates from first principles

title: phono3py — lattice thermal conductivity
why: Computes κ_L from third-order force constants, the missing ingredient for predicting zT.

title: Wannier90 — maximally-localized Wannier functions
why: Builds tight-binding models from DFT, the first step for surface states and Wilson loops.

title: WannierTools — topological analysis of Wannier models
why: Computes Z2 indices, Weyl points, surface spectra and Fermi arcs to compare with ARPES.

ref.title: WannierTools: An open-source software package for novel topological materials

title: Z2Pack — topological invariants from Wannier charge centers
why: Automated, robust calculation of Z2 and Chern numbers.

ref.title: Z2Pack: Numerical implementation of hybrid Wannier centers for identifying topological materials

title: IrRep — irreducible representations of DFT bands
why: Extracts the symmetry data that symmetry-indicator / TQC classifications need.

title: PythTB — Python tight binding
why: Small, readable tight-binding package for learning Berry phases and Chern numbers hands-on.

title: SeeK-path — band-structure k-paths
why: Gives the standard Brillouin-zone path and labels for any structure, useful for reading band plots and ARPES cuts.

title: Materials Project documentation
why: Explains how MP structures, energies above hull and band gaps are calculated.

title: Materials Project workshop notebooks
why: Hands-on notebooks for querying and analysing MP data with pymatgen.

title: JARVIS-Tools example notebooks
why: Notebooks on the JARVIS-DFT data used here, including spillage and transport.

title: OPTIMADE — one API for many materials databases
why: The open standard this atlas uses to query Materials Project, Alexandria, OQMD and COD.

ref.title: OPTIMADE, an API for exchanging materials data

title: Topological Materials Database (Topological Quantum Chemistry)
why: Look up the symmetry-indicator topological classification of any ICSD compound.

title: Materiae — topological materials database
why: Independent high-throughput topological classification (IOP-CAS), useful to cross-check TQC.

title: Bilbao Crystallographic Server
why: Space-group tables, Wyckoff positions, k-vector types and band representations.

title: Crystallography Open Database
why: Open experimental crystal structures. It is the source of the "experiment" column on every material page.

ref.title: Crystallography Open Database – an open-access collection of crystal structures
